hyps.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 receives no input, so edge 4 carries nothing and the conv edit gives almost no gain.
Edge 2 starts at node 1, which is disconnected when edge 0 is none, so the edit is nearly inert.
Without edge 1, edge 5 is reachable only via the longer path through edges 0 and 2, so its conv gain is diluted.
Replacing none with a conv on the direct input-output edge adds a whole new learnable path, a bigger gain than upgrading an existing op.
Replacing none with a conv on edge 1 creates a new path, which helps more than replacing an op already there.
A skip on edge 4 only matters if node 1 carries a signal, which requires edge 0 to be active.
Adding a conv where there was no edge into the output gives a larger gain than swapping one op for another.
Replacing none with a conv on edge 0 activates the downstream edges 2 and 4, which gives a large gain.
Removing a 3x3 conv from the direct edge loses much more accuracy than removing a weaker op such as pooling or skip.
Deleting a 3x3 conv feeding the output hurts more than deleting a weaker op there.
